summary: Ran a grep census for theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom over all 50 changed/added files in this unit; every file matched at least one declaration keyword, none is a zero-declaration candidate. File sizes range from 1.4KB to 68.7KB, consistent with substantive Lean content rather than stubs. All 50 files live under FLT/ (AutomorphicForm, DedekindDomain, Deformations, DivisionAlgebra, GlobalLanglandsConjectures, HaarMeasure, HenselianLocalRing, KnownIn1980s, Mathlib (upstreamable auxiliary lemmas), NumberField, Patching, QuaternionAlgebra, and Slop), the same substantive FLT/FLTTest formalization tree the prior review (RRV-6437176b31bd-r1) already retained; none touches the already-excluded blueprint-verso/ Verso presentation subtree or the three already-excluded empty planning/TODO stubs (FLT/GroupScheme/FiniteFlat.lean, FLT/Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Completion.lean, FLT/TateCurve/TateCurve.lean), which are unchanged and not renamed here. Read the largest new file, FLT/Slop/PGL2/FiniteSubgroups/CyclicPartition.lean, in full header/doc-comment: its own file comment explains the FLT/Slop namespace holds code ported from an external project that does not yet follow mathlib style-linter conventions -- not junk or scratch content -- and the file itself is a real classification-theory development (Dickson.HasCyclicPartition, isCyclic_of_hasCyclicPartition, dihedral_of_hasCyclicPartition_odd/even, iso_A4/S4/A5_of_hasCyclicPartition) toward Dickson's classification of finite subgroups of PGL2. No file in this unit meets the FILTER-002/FILTER-004 evidence bar for exclusion. Retain all 50.

summary: All 19 files in this work unit contain substantial formal mathematical content — definitions, lemmas, theorems, and proofs — relevant to the FLT formalization. They cover Hecke operators on quaternionic automorphic forms, Galois theory (Frobenius elements, infinite Galois correspondence), elliptic curve variable changes, group theory (cyclic groups), linear algebra (determinants in central simple algebras), measure theory (unimodular groups, Haar measure), p-adic height one spectrum, patching algebra/module theory (Taylor-Wiles-Kisin method), adic topology, module depth/Krull dimension, Dickson's classification of finite subgroups of PGL₂, and representation theory (irreducible vs absolutely irreducible). None are empty stubs, pure import aggregators, documentation, or otherwise lacking formal mathematical declarations. All should remain in the primary search index.
